clue.text: Inform about road options, by the sound of it, for ordinary people

parts.note: to grass is British slang for informing on someone to the police

indicators.note: says the routes are heard rather than written, giving a word spoken the same way

parts.note: routes are the roads one may choose between

explanation.surface: A tip-off about which roads to take, offered for the benefit of ordinary folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the sound of it' turns ROUTES into ROOTS, said the same way. GRASS is British slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: The grassroots are the rank and file of a movement or party, the ordinary members rather than leaders.

clue.text: Attempt to join RAF on way up? Succeed

parts.note: a go is an attempt

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read in reverse

explanation.surface: A recruit tries to join the Royal Air Force and climb the ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: To go far is an idiom for achieving success in life.

clue.text: Vegetable a chore — Kit harassed

indicators.note: something harassed is disturbed, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Kit is harassed by a chore involving vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: An artichoke is a vegetable, the edible flower bud of a thistle-like plant.

clue.text: Victory in southeast he's referred to with contempt

indicators.note: says the word for victory sits inside the compass abbreviation

parts.note: a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A man who triumphs in the southeast is spoken of scornfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Swine is a term of abuse for a contemptible person.

clue.text: Public not allowed

definitions.meaning: ... means known publicly, as a secret that is ...

explanation.definitionFit: Out covers both revealed to everyone and excluded or not permitted.

clue.text: Row of houses in sketch, engaging Queen

indicators.note: the sketch word holds the Queen's letters inside it

parts.note: to trace is to sketch or draw over
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A drawing of a terrace with the Queen in it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a terrace is a continuous row of joined houses.

clue.text: One often finishing second misread bid unfortunately

indicators.note: an unlucky result here suggests the letters landing in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A runner-up misjudged a bid, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'always the bridesmaid, never the bride', for someone always second.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridesmaid attends the bride, so proverbially comes second to her, never the main figure.

clue.text: Soccer official, Italian, works to improve

parts.note: ref is short for referee
It is short for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: A football referee from Italy carries out improvement work.
explanation.definitionFit: To refit is to overhaul or renovate something, doing work on it to make it better.

clue.text: Temporary home period I included

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: says the letter I is placed within the word for period

parts.note: a term is a period of time, as at school

explanation.surface: A temporary home for a term, with me included.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim arrangement is a provisional one, standing only until a permanent one is made.

clue.text: Manufacturer of timepieces with new start becomes go-between for couples

indicators.note: the opening letter is swapped for a different one

parts.note: a watchmaker makes timepieces

explanation.surface: A clockmaker starts afresh as a dating agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with new start' replaces the W of WATCHMAKER with M.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchmaker arranges romantic pairings, acting as an intermediary between prospective partners.

clue.text: After scandal, man accommodating English at very low price

parts.note: dirt is scandalous gossip

indicators.note: the man's word takes in the letter for English, holding it inside

parts.note: chap is a British informal word for a man

explanation.surface: After a scandal, a man takes in an Englishman for a pittance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dirt-cheap costs very little, an idiom for a bargain price.

clue.text: Vigil peer arranged? That's right

indicators.note: these letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A lord holding a vigil asks whether that is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A privilege is a special right or advantage granted to someone.

clue.text: Part of cap that is fitting

indicators.note: signals the answer is a portion of the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A piece of the cap is the bit that fits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' points to letters running across 'cap that'.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt means suitable or appropriate, a synonym for fitting.

clue.text: Speech one's rewritten — about Royal Marines

indicators.note: says the rearranged letters go around the abbreviation for the marines
letters written again in a new order signal an anagram

explanation.surface: Someone redrafts their speech about the Royal Marines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' gives SEON, and 'about' wraps it round the marines' abbreviation; the apostrophe in one's is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A sermon is a speech, typically a religious address given from a pulpit.

clue.text: Rhode Island job, attractive ultimately, gets quick response

parts.note: RI is the US postal abbreviation for Rhode Island
a post is a job

indicators.note: the last letter of attractive is taken

explanation.surface: An attractive job in Rhode Island draws a swift reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, sharp retort, originally a fencing counterthrust.

clue.text: Greeting detective, we hear, in advanced style

parts.note: hi is a greeting

indicators.note: says the detective's short word stands for another word said the same way

parts.note: tec is short for detective

explanation.surface: Saying hello to a detective, apparently, in a sophisticated manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' makes TEC stand for TECH, which sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Hi-tech describes a modern design style using industrial materials and advanced technology.

clue.text: High mountain with a lake and parking

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A tall peak beside a lake, with a car park.
explanation.definitionFit: An alp is a high mountain, from the Alps of Switzerland and neighbours.

clue.text: Needing no introduction, wench one lad's seen with — a Mexican dish!

indicators.note: losing the introduction means the word wench drops its first letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wench, who needs no introduction, is seen with a lad over a Mexican dish.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a tortilla rolled round a filling and baked in chilli sauce, a staple of Mexican cooking.

clue.text: Confident contribution from medic and orderly

indicators.note: contribution from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A doctor and a hospital orderly both bring self-assurance.
explanation.definitionFit: A can-do attitude is positive and self-assured, ready to tackle anything.

clue.text: Worry as new gaffer sets tasks at the outset

indicators.note: takes the first letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Anxiety as a new boss hands out jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: A gaffer is British slang for a boss or manager.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is deep anxiety or dread, a synonym of worry.

clue.text: Realise daughter is at Church — remain on outside

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: the outside letters of remain are placed on the end

explanation.surface: A daughter realises she is at church, staying on outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To discern something is to perceive or recognise it, a synonym of realise.

clue.text: Female's oeuvre oddly ignored

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A woman's body of work is strangely overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve, the first woman in Genesis, stands in crosswords for any female.

clue.text: Bird, better than birdie?

definitions.meaning: in golf an ... is two under par, one better than a birdie

explanation.surface: Asking which bird beats a birdie.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle is both a raptor and a golf score two strokes under par.

clue.text: Friendly event noble recollected

indicators.note: collected again into a different order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A noble fondly remembers a pleasant occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' looks like memory but signals rearranging EVENT NOBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Benevolent means kindly and well-meaning, close to friendly.
